links.comparator_used: Radiologists assessing bone age independently without AI assistance (crossover design)
links.outcome: Bone age assessment accuracy (mean absolute difference from expert ground truth; proportion of estimates with MAD >1 year)
links.effect: MAD 0.74 vs 0.46 years without vs with AI (p < 0.001); proportion of assessments with MAD >1 year 24.0% vs 8.4% (p < 0.001); improved predictions with AI 16.8% vs less accurate predictions with AI 2.3% (p < 0.001)
links.tradeoff: Automation bias was prone to affect less experienced radiologists; 2.3% of predictions became less accurate with AI assistance. Senior radiologists disagreed with the AI more often. No consistent timing effect between early and delayed AI assistance.
links.quote: The AI algorithm improved the BA assessment accuracy of radiologists with varying experience levels.

design_hint: AI assistance with clinician review and override; timing of AI assistance (early vs delayed)
